title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

reading.body:
This is a case of a system used outside the conditions it was built for. Access to law enforcement databases and camera systems is granted for policing purposes, and the alleged conduct here is personal use of that access to locate and follow one individual. The failure sits at the point of authorised access rather than at the point of any model or automated decision, so no technical control on the database itself would have flagged it as anomalous.

Catching this kind of misuse requires auditing who queried which records and why, and comparing that pattern against the casework that justified the access. The reporting describes an investigation that followed the conduct, not a check that preceded or interrupted it. Whether any such audit existed before the investigation began is not established.

The charges are allegations. An indictment is not a conviction, and the reporting does not establish guilt, intent, or what internal oversight, if any, was in place at the time.

reports.title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

summary:
A former Coffee County sheriff’s deputy, Chris Ashley Rozar, 49, has been released on bond after a grand jury indicted him on eight counts, including four counts of violation of oath by a public officer, two counts of computer invasion of privacy, one count of prohibited use of captured license plate data, and one count of stalking. Investigators say Rozar misused law enforcement databases and camera systems for personal reasons, and the stalking charge alleges he tracked and surveilled a woman without her consent. He was terminated when the investigation began.

The woman involved spoke anonymously, saying she waited two years for the investigation and hopes her story encourages other women to report abuse. Rozar was arrested on May 5 and released on bond the same day. He is scheduled for arraignment on May 27 in Coffee County Superior Court.
